definition: Qualitative data are the detailed, information-rich material collected in qualitative research, often from open-ended interviews, that supports deep, case-focused analysis and a richer understanding of the topic being studied. Its value depends on how much useful information each participant’s account provides.

reasons: The packet does not support the claim that qualitative data are “detailed, information-rich material”; those exact descriptive phrases (or an equivalent explicit characterization) are not stated in the provided text.
The packet supports “deep, case-oriented analysis” (via Sandelowski) but does not explicitly support the definition’s claim of a “richer understanding of the topic being studied.”

The packet does support parts of the definition about open-ended/open-question interviewing producing “richer data,” and it supports the idea that the amount of useful/usable data per person affects how many participants are needed (Morse), which aligns with the definition’s second sentence. However, these partial matches do not fully validate the unsupported descriptive/general claims in the first sentence.
